PyTorch distinguishes evaluation mode from gradient disabling: `eval()` disables dropout; `no_grad()` prevents graph construction. For mining, save `was_training = model.training`, call `model.eval()`, then inside `torch.no_grad()` recompute encoder features from the same masked inputs, score eligible candidates in chunks, and retain detached top-k item IDs. Exclude padding, the reserved mask token, positives and prohibited training-history items. Use `try/finally: model.train(was_training)` to restore mode reliably. During optimization, ensure training mode, recompute features with gradients enabled, and rescore selected IDs through the actual item embeddings. Detached mining scores/features must not replace differentiable training scores. Preserve target masking and appended-mask inference; use the final nonpadding position for left-padded terminal inputs. [PyTorch autograd documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/autograd)

Implementation cost inference: each distinct masked input requires one evaluation/no-grad encoder forward plus one training forward and backward, versus one forward/backward without mining. Separate terminal and Cloze inputs therefore require four forwards and two backwards, unless batched together. Reusing dropout-enabled training features for detached selection avoids the extra encoder forward but changes mining behavior. Candidate chunking bounds mining-score memory; maintain a running top-k instead of concatenating every score. Runtime overhead includes candidate scoring and cannot be inferred from encoder counts alone.

For memory-safe training, zero gradients once, recompute each input microbatch, backward its weighted loss immediately, and step once after all chunks. Preserve `λ_terminal·sum(loss_terminal)/N_terminal + λ_cloze·sum(loss_cloze)/N_cloze`, using original denominators, rather than averaging chunk means equally. Merely summing differentiable chunk losses retains their graphs. Repeated backwards through shared encoder features requires graph retention; independent microbatch graphs avoid that. Splitting a softmax candidate axis requires a global normalizer, not independent chunk softmaxes. [PyTorch backward documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.autograd.backward.html)
